Class FramedEyeGameTestsLogic

java.lang.Object
com.github.crittscott.somegoogly.gametest.FramedEyeGameTestsLogic
public final class FramedEyeGameTestsLogic extends Object
Drives the mounted eye simulation without a client renderer. Actual frame mounting, render-context isolation, lighting, pause, and unloading require the in-game checks in docs/framed-eyes-testing.md.

  • Method Details

    • framedEyeFiltersItems

      public static void framedEyeFiltersItems(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Only a Googly Eye in a frame gets a moving pupil; a Slimy Eye, an ordinary item, and an empty frame get none. In game: frame a Googly Eye, then replace it with a Slimy Eye, then a diamond, then nothing; only the Googly Eye's pupil moves.

    • framedEyeFollowsMountedGravity

      public static void framedEyeFollowsMountedGravity(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A framed eye's pupil falls toward the ground however the frame or the item in it is turned. In game: frame a Googly Eye on a wall and right-click it to rotate it through each position; its pupil always settles at the bottom.

    • framedEyeHandlesShortIntervalsAndTimeJumps

      public static void framedEyeHandlesShortIntervalsAndTimeJumps(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Expressions never overlap, even with the shortest ambient interval, and an eye seen again after a long absence joins the expression now playing. In game: set ambientMinTicks = 1 and ambientMaxTicks = 1 and ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:blink"] in somegoogly-server.toml, then /reload; a framed Googly Eye blinks back to back, each blink finishing before the next starts.

    • framedEyeHonorsAmbientSettings

      public static void framedEyeHonorsAmbientSettings(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A framed eye stops expressing, even mid-expression, when ambient expressions are off, the pool is empty, or the pool holds only expressions that need a second eye. In game: with ambientMinTicks = 1 and ambientMaxTicks = 1 and ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:blink"] in somegoogly-server.toml, watch a framed Googly Eye blink. Then set each in turn and /reload: ambientBehaviors = false; ambientBehaviorPool = []; ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:cross_eye"]. Each time the eye stops blinking and plays nothing.

    • framedEyePlaysSingleEyeExpressions

      public static void framedEyePlaysSingleEyeExpressions(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A lone eye skips expressions that need a partner and still plays the rest. In game: set ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:cross_eye", "somegoogly:blink"] in somegoogly-server.toml and /reload; a framed Googly Eye winks from time to time and never tries to cross.

    • framedEyeReconstructsExpressions

      public static void framedEyeReconstructsExpressions(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A player who starts watching a frame mid-expression sees the same expression at the same point as everyone else. In game: with two players, have one watch a framed Googly Eye while the other approaches from out of render range; when it comes into view, both see the same expression at the same moment.

    • framedEyeReleasesExpressionOverlays

      public static void framedEyeReleasesExpressionOverlays(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Each expression ends fully, leaving the eye as it was. In game: set ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:blink"] in somegoogly-server.toml and /reload; between blinks a framed Googly Eye opens fully to its normal size.

    • framedEyeUsesIndependentSchedules

      public static void framedEyeUsesIndependentSchedules(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      Each frame keeps its own expression schedule, even when frames hold identical eyes. In game: fill several neighboring frames with Googly Eyes from one stack; they blink and glance at different times.

    • framedHeadAllowsPairedExpressions

      public static void framedHeadAllowsPairedExpressions(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A framed eyed head's two eyes can cross toward each other; a lone Googly Eye under the same settings cannot. In game: set ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:cross_eye"] and ambientMinTicks = 1 and ambientMaxTicks = 1 in somegoogly-server.toml and /reload, then frame an eyed skeleton skull beside a Googly Eye; the skull's pupils cross and the lone eye stays still.

    • framedHeadInvalidatesChangedItems

      public static void framedHeadInvalidatesChangedItems(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A framed head's eyes follow what the frame now holds: a different species, eye arrangement, or appearance gets a fresh layout, and a plain head or a loose eye shows nothing of the head before it. In game: frame an eyed skeleton skull, then swap in an eyed creeper head, an eyed skeleton skull with glowing eyes, a plain skull, and a Googly Eye; each shows only its own eyes, if any.

    • framedHeadReconstructsExpressions

      public static void framedHeadReconstructsExpressions(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A player who starts watching a framed head mid-blink sees the same eyes blinking at the same point as everyone else. In game: with two players and ambientBehaviorPool = ["somegoogly:blink"] in somegoogly-server.toml, have one watch a framed eyed skeleton skull while the other approaches from out of render range; both see each blink together.

    • framedHeadUsesConfiguredLayout

      public static void framedHeadUsesConfiguredLayout(net.minecraft.gametest.framework.GameTestHelper helper)
      A framed eyed head shows its mob's eyes where they sit on the placed head, with its stored appearance, and its pupils fall toward the ground. In game: frame an eyed skeleton skull, and with the Heads mod installed an eyed Heads-mod head; each shows its eyes in the same places, colors, and sizes as when placed, and the pupils move.
